At around 1:00am last night I decided I was going to give a crack at a Youtube replacement. The core philosophy of it is to treat all content the same. It is 100% built from scratch in node.

What got coded in those hours:
A front-end file splitter and uploader.
A signin / user system
An http 206 implementation that if more correct that the other node 206 code kicking around
A "Smart LRU", more about that in a bit
Responsive video size mimicking Youtube's.

All code is 100% asynchronous, which it needs to be. This is partially an experiment to see what $2 a month worth of hardware can do. There are 15 Gigs on the drive and I'm willing to let Voat have it. What should really function well with Voat is the Smart LRU.

It assigns every video a score based on recent view count. When the drive reaches 90% capacity it kicks the video with the lowest score compared to it's size. This means that big videos that people always want to watch stay around. Small videos that people rarely watch but want archived stay around. The front page always stays around, but large videos that never make it on to the front page of Voat or Reddit die. Up to 90% of the content uploaded on the web is completely idle and really never got viewed in the first place.

Why is this important? Internet freedom without people donating to sites depends on aggressive cost savings. The fact that the average person can't readily replace Youtube means that those that fund it at the end of the day get their say, and at the exculusion of your free speech.

This brings us to content policy. If it is a video, isn't illegal and doesn't get DCMA'd it belongs there. All video content will be treated equal if offensive, lewd, funny, reasonable, unreasonable, features guns, or even is problematic. Anyone who complains at your content can just deal.

This means that the site will likely never get advertising dollars which is why the experiment of how low can you go with hardware is important. I have no problem expanding it's hardware... substantially. But let's see what does happen when you go with something literally anyone could run.
